note: The administered German is the official WHOQOL-BREF German version (ATHIS 2014 module) and is left exactly as published. The English shipped in the _translated columns is the WHO's own published English WHOQOL-BREF wording for the same numbered items, not a fresh rendering of the German -- e.g. LQ4 carries WHO's 'How much do you need any medical treatment to function in your daily life?'. That is a parallel official version rather than a translation of this text, which is better wording but a different provenance claim, so it is recorded as such. instrument, instructions and all four section prompts are translated rather than sourced, because WHO publishes no parallel for the ATHIS framing.

An adapted Chinese Insomnia Severity Index: the interference item names study efficiency rather than the ISI original's work and chores, so the administered Chinese is translated here rather than substituting the published ISI English, which would not correspond word-for-word. instructions and option_text are already English in the published table and their _translated columns stay empty.
Macleod Clark Professional Identity Scale adapted to rehabilitation practice; option_text is already English so only item_text carries a translation.
Claremont Purpose Scale, Chinese administration. Each item has its own labelled 5-point scale, so all 45 distinct anchors are translated individually rather than through one shared set.
49-item technology-assisted EFL self-regulation questionnaire, author-written; only the two endpoint anchors are named.

Chinese FAD-Plus (Paulhus & Carey 2011). Published English exists for the FAD-Plus, but the Chinese item set here does not map one-to-one onto it -- dataset2 carries ten items absent from dataset1, including soul/mind items -- so the administered Chinese is translated rather than a numbering correspondence being asserted that was not verified.
As fad_dataset1; the ten extra items are translated on the same basis.
Adolescent Self-Rating Life Events Checklist, a Chinese-origin instrument. instructions and option_text are already English in the published table, so only item_text carries a translation.
Chinese Duesseldorf Orthorexia Scale. Item codes carry the source numbering inside the text ("4. ...") and are left verbatim in the base field, numbering included.

Champion's Breast Cancer Fear Scale, Spanish administration. option_text is already English in the published table (the mismatch already flagged on the issues page), so only item_text carries a translation.

Launay-Slade Hallucination Scale - Extended, Spanish. Published English exists for the LSHS-E but this administration is a Spanish adaptation with its own 0-4 anchor wording, so the administered text is translated rather than the original substituted.

BDI-II, Spanish administration. The sourcing rule is deliberately NOT applied here: the official English BDI-II wording is Pearson-licensed, so the _translated column is our own rendering of the Spanish statements the study published, not Beck's published English. Compound options where the source joins two statements with ';' (appetite and sleep items) are kept as one string in both columns so the base and translation stay row-aligned.

UWES-17, Polish version. All 17 Polish items map one-to-one onto Schaufeli & Bakker's published English UWES-17 (6 vigour, 5 dedication, 6 absorption), so the official English is shipped. option_text is already English in the published table.
Oldenburg Burnout Inventory, Polish version, 8-item form administered. Items map onto Demerouti's published English OLBI. option_text is already English.

Basic Psychological Need Satisfaction and Frustration Scale at Work, Polish version. Published English exists (Chen et al.) but this is a work-domain adaptation whose 24 items were not verified one-to-one against it, so the administered Polish is translated instead. Source typos kept verbatim in the base field ('w prazy' for 'w pracy'; the spaced 'związany/ a', 'pewny/ a').

Job Crafting Scale, Polish version. As bpnsf: Tims, Bakker & Derks' English exists but the correspondence was not verified item by item, so the Polish is translated. Stray spacing before punctuation is left as published ('o radę .', 'Staram się , aby').
